processing: Typical of Fenghuang Dancong: sun-withered, shaken and rested to partial oxidation, fired, rolled and dried or lightly roasted.
harvest_season: As with most Fenghuang Dancong, spring is the main picking.
appearance_dry: Typically long, dark brown strips, as with other Dancong.
appearance_liquor: Typically clear orange-yellow, as with other Dancong.
appearance_wet: Typically long leaves, green with reddened edges, as with other Dancong.
taste_profile: Little is documented on this bush's own cup. Its zhilan group is known for a clear, elegant orchid aroma.

brewing.notes: As with other Dancong, keep the leaf load modest and pour off quickly.

vintage_note: Rarely listed. As is usual for Dancong, it is sold by spring harvest of the current year, often with some months of rest after roasting.
description:
Ji Long Kan is a Fenghuang Dancong named for its shape: the tree's form is said to look like a farmhouse chicken coop. A similar naming habit, based on how a tree looks rather than how the tea smells, shows up with several other Fenghuang bushes.

Chinese writing on Dancong groups places it with the zhilan (orchid) aroma type, which is a useful guide to what to expect, since little is written about this bush itself.

It would be made like other Dancong, by sun withering, shaking, firing and rolling. As for the group in general, look for a clear orchid aroma, and brew with short steeps.

It is a rare name in shops. Ask the seller which trees the leaf came from, and compare it against a more common zhilan Dancong if you can.
history: Little is documented beyond the origin of its name. When the bush was first singled out, and by whom, is not recorded in anything readily available.
